Sentence (English): Pros:.
Comments (English): Pros:. It's extremely quiet and cleans well on Heavy with Zone Booster. Cons:. I purchased this on July 31 and today is September 11. I installed it the day after it arrived. The next day, I found a large puddle around my island. After work, I doubled checked my installation and then called Home Depot. Unfortunately, self-install voided any sort of warranty through Home Depot, so I got redirected to Samsung. I ran out of time, so I had to call back again the next day. I'm now outside of the 48 delivery window, and firmly into Samsung's one-year warranty. Here is my explanation to Samsung's customer service. Heavy with Zone Booster leaks so much that it almost always triggers an error, "LC", and the dishwasher stops mid cycle. Normal with no Zone Booster will usually make it through a cycle but it doesn't clean very well. The dishwasher is in the open in the middle of my kitchen, surrounded by towels. The leak is coming from underneath the dishwasher and not the water inlet or drain, the only two hoses that I installed. After an hour on the phone, Samsung eventually had me unplug the dishwaher, wait, and the plug it in again to reset the leak "LC" error. To them, the problem was fixed, and the phonecall ended. Another hour on the phone and I did the same thing and asked for a service technician. I was provided a broken link to sign up for one. Another hour on the phone and Samsung arranged for a technician to come to my house on August 22. The technician quickly removed a side panel and found factory installed hoses not properly connected and "perhaps" a broken part. He then said he ordered the replacement part and would reschedule after it arrived. Had I removed the panel, my Samsung warranty would have been in jeopardy. Tomorrow, September 12, is a full three weeks since the technician came. I haven't heard a peep from either Samsung or the technician. Hurricane Idalia hit on August 30 so I decided to wait longer to hear from them. I'll be calling Samsung again today to try to see what my repair status is. I expect it to take another hour on the phone. Note: I wasn't exaggerating each time I said an hour on the phone. Samsung makes you start from the beginning each and every call. Time it yourself after you buy this dishwasher. You'll get really good at unplugging the dishwasher, checking the inlet, checking the garbage disposal, etc.

Sentence (English): We bought this Kitchenaid dishwasher with the FreeFlex Third rack a couple of months ago after two bad experiences with the Bosch 300 and Bosch 500 (both returned for failing to perform to expectations).
Comments (English): [ Finally! A great dishwasher ] || ---------------- || We bought this Kitchenaid dishwasher with the FreeFlex Third rack a couple of months ago after two bad experiences with the Bosch 300 and Bosch 500 (both returned for failing to perform to expectations). We LOVE this dishwasher, especially the FreeFlex Third Rack. Unlike other third racks we've seen, that can only hold very small or flat items, the FreeFlex holds bowls, mugs, glasses, and even has a removeable rack for silverware. It makes a huge difference in being able to fill the dishwasher before the second rack fills up with mugs, bowls and glasses. Best of all, the dishes are spotless and fully dry -- even the plastic -- after every load. The salesperson said that most customers want either a Bosch or a Kitchenaid, and she preferred the Kitchenaid because it had an internal drying system instead of an external (outside the tub) like the Bosch -- I wish we'd listened to her! In our experience, the Kitchenaid is far superior.

Sentence (English): We ordered this thing after decades of living without a dishwasher, and when I tell you we were counting down the days until it arrived, honey, I mean the countdown was mentioned every single day multiple times.
Comments (English): [ This tiny powerhouse changes lives! ] || ---------------- || We ordered this thing after decades of living without a dishwasher, and when I tell you we were counting down the days until it arrived, honey, I mean the countdown was mentioned every single day multiple times. When we got down to the last 2 days, I started worrying that I'd exaggerated the impact our post-Bosch existence would truly have. Did we use enough dishes to warrant one of these? Would we really gain back multiple hours a week that had previously been reserved for handwashing everything from dinner to meal prep for our lunches as teachers? Would I use those regained hours for reading novels on a treadmill and picking up meditation? Would we be better people with more patience for each other and our students? I am here 1.5 months post-Bosch to tell you that YES, this tiny, shiny thing has helped us realize all these dreams AND MORE. Knowing I don't have to spend as much time for cleanup means my cooking ambitions are more expansive than ever because I no longer make decisions based on using as few utensils and tools as possible! Instead of after-dinner dread and slogging through cleanup, we're finally going to bed on time and feeling like working in schools is actually sustainable. As a nighttime shower person, I set this lil' guy on a 1-hr delay just in case our old house has feelings about using water in two places at a time (not even sure if it does! ). We test it because we can't believe that anything would possibly clean this smoothie cup that sat in the car over the weekend, and it surprises us each time.It's as quiet as they say, it fits perfectly in our super small kitchen, and we fit way more dishes in there than I thought would be possible. Our stuff comes out remarkably clean, and the controls are easy and self-explanatory even for someone who doesn't download a PDF of the manual weeks ahead of time out of excitement. I even stuck a magnetic towel bar on it so I didn't have to leave the sink to dry my hands! A review here convinced me that this was the move, and I'm SO grateful we went with it.

Sentence (English): I've always been interested in dishwashers, but the built-in type requires cutting the bottom of the island countertop because the sink is low.
Comments (English): [ No installation, no touch, 3-person dishwasher! ] || ---------------- || I've always been interested in dishwashers, but the built-in type requires cutting the bottom of the island countertop because the sink is low. And since the dishwasher would eliminate the already scarce shelf space, I was just thinking about getting one. But... I won the Coupang Experience Group, so I got to try the non-installation type, which is installed on top! Let's compare it to a regular dishwasher to see what its advantages are. ## Product Name: Media Electric Dishwasher for 3 People, MD-32BK Black, Self-Installation Type. ## Product Description: . 1) Capacity: For 3 people or less. 2) Function: Sterilization + Drying. 3) Size: Slightly large at 435mm wide x 420mm deep x 435mm high. 4) Product Weight: 14kg. 5) Power Consumption: 730W. 6) Detailed Description: - Convenient to use without installation. Just connect the drain hose and plug in the cord and you're done! - 72-hour ventilation circulation system, from drying to safe storage! > The drying function is improved by installing a fan inside the product, and the airflow is generated for 72 hours to remove moisture and odor! - 360-degree storm shower with two-stage high-pressure rotation water spray! > The powerful water spray and 360-degree rotation create a stream of water that sprays water into every corner without leaving any blind spots. - 72-degree high-temperature water thoroughly removes even grease! - 5 practical washing modes! - The automatic water level recognition sensor automatically sounds an alarm when the internal water tank is full. - It has a water tray, so it can be used anywhere, such as under the sink or on an upper cabinet, but it must be able to drain. 7) Internal structure: - It has easy-to-install wheels. - Washable filter and strainer. - Convenient detergent dispenser (no lid). ## User review. - It seems to be just right for 3 people. - It can be used for rice bowls, soup bowls, plates (except for the sunken ones) and spoons. - I wash things like pots, frying pans, and bowls and run the dishwasher for the rest, so it saves a lot of time. - The standard mode's cleaning power removes grease, but it doesn't clean stuck-on items like spatulas! - The noise level is good if you don't use it at night, and it's about the same as everyday noise during the day. - Make sure to turn on the power when refilling water! Otherwise, an alarm will sound. It's annoying. I will use it well. Thank you. This is a purchase review written after receiving the product for free as part of a Coupang Experience Group event.

Since I have children, I often use dishwasher-safe plastic dishes, plates, and cups. They say they washed dishes by hand before purchasing a dishwasher. The plastic was very difficult to clean off the grease. No matter how thoroughly you washed the dishes, there were times when the slippery texture just wouldn't go away. I was impressed when I ran the dishwasher. It cleans really well! We are a family of 4 with 2 babies and toddlers, and everything went in, including a large pot, dishes for 1-2 meals, cooking utensils, and a cutting board. My back hurt, my knees hurt, and the soles of my feet hurt. After using the dishwasher for a day, I regret why I bought it only now. If you have the space to install it in your kitchen, it is an absolute must-have item. Even if you don't have it, make space and install it. It will really improve your quality of life. However, the downside is that it is a bit noisy, so I am a bit worried about the noise between floors at night. Other than that, I haven't found any flaws yet.

Sentence (English): We ordered this thing after decades of living without a dishwasher, and when I tell you we were counting down the days until it arrived, honey, I mean the countdown was mentioned every single day multiple times.
Comments (English): [ This tiny powerhouse changes lives! ] || ---------------- || We ordered this thing after decades of living without a dishwasher, and when I tell you we were counting down the days until it arrived, honey, I mean the countdown was mentioned every single day multiple times. When we got down to the last 2 days, I started worrying that I'd exaggerated the impact our post-Bosch existence would truly have. Did we use enough dishes to warrant one of these? Would we really gain back multiple hours a week that had previously been reserved for handwashing everything from dinner to meal prep for our lunches as teachers? Would I use those regained hours for reading novels on a treadmill and picking up meditation? Would we be better people with more patience for each other and our students? I am here 1.5 months post-Bosch to tell you that YES, this tiny, shiny thing has helped us realize all these dreams AND MORE. Knowing I don't have to spend as much time for cleanup means my cooking ambitions are more expansive than ever because I no longer make decisions based on using as few utensils and tools as possible! Instead of after-dinner dread and slogging through cleanup, we're finally going to bed on time and feeling like working in schools is actually sustainable. As a nighttime shower person, I set this lil' guy on a 1-hr delay just in case our old house has feelings about using water in two places at a time (not even sure if it does! ). We test it because we can't believe that anything would possibly clean this smoothie cup that sat in the car over the weekend, and it surprises us each time. It's as quiet as they say, it fits perfectly in our super small kitchen, and we fit way more dishes in there than I thought would be possible. Our stuff comes out remarkably clean, and the controls are easy and self-explanatory even for someone who doesn't download a PDF of the manual weeks ahead of time out of excitement. I even stuck a magnetic towel bar on it so I didn't have to leave the sink to dry my hands! A review here convinced me that this was the move, and I'm SO grateful we went with it.

Sentence (English): Fantastic dishwasher!
Comments (English): [ Fantastic dishwasher / awful installation process ] || ---------------- || Fantastic dishwasher! Super quiet! It cleans our dishes and pots, including tea stains incredibly well. I highly recommend Bosch dishwashers. Whoever I spoke with, who also has a Bosch dishwasher, is very satisfied with their dishwasher. However, we had a very bad experience with the 'At Your Service' company that Costco hires to install the product. Three plumbers came within a week. The first one didn't even move the old dishwasher and told us that we had to have a split valve, which was contradicted by the 2nd plumber, who seemed to be really skilled. However, due to another problem not mentioned by the first plumber since he didn't check anything, a 3rd plumber had to come and for him everything under our sink seemed to be a problem. He left without installing the product. Therefore, overall, we had 3 unsuccessful installation visits and ended up hiring someone else paying extra money for the installation and the unnecessary split valve that was supposedly required. Costco reimbursed us partially for this installation. Our neighbors had a similar bad experience with the same At Your Service company after they purchased a dryer from Costco. I think that Costco should consider changing the company that does installations for them.

Sentence (English): The new dishwasher failed to dry, even when "Extra Dry" was selected.
Comments (English): [ Not a happy camper.  ] || ---------------- || The new dishwasher failed to dry, even when "Extra Dry" was selected. I called the Bosch customer support line and was guided through a series of choices, using the control panel selection buttons. I was assured that this reset needed to be done only once, and that everything should be fine. There was no change. I expect plastic items to need air-drying, after running a load in the dishwasher. I realize there may be a bit of water in rimmed items, such as a ceramic mug. But hardly any items are dry, after each cycle is completed, including beverage glasses, ceramic bowls, and flatware. The top rack for utensils and flatware is useless. I stopped using the top rack when I realized that some items were not getting clean, let alone dry. The spacers to hold items on the middle and bottom racks are poorly designed. They are too close together and best suited for thin plates and saucers. Measuring cups, bowls, and casserole dishes are difficult to position and space is wasted. This leads to more frequent use of the dishwasher, with the added cost of using extra power, water, and detergent.

Sentence (English): This is the 4th dishwasher I've had over the last 10 years between 3 houses.
Comments (English): [ Best dishwasher experience I didn't know I could ] || ---------------- || This is the 4th dishwasher I've had over the last 10 years between 3 houses. I never gave much thought to the dishwasher since they 'worked'. After having this in place and used I realized there is so many levels to 'work'. Sure my dishes were clean, but never this clean. The amount of things that have washed to such a pristine condition blows my mind. I have had glass cups for years and the first run through this and they looked as crystal clear as when they were brand new. I forgot how clear they were capable of being, even from hand a washing. The third row top tray is fantastic to clean odd shaded utensils and lids and can't believe I've lived without it for so long. The water jets specifically for cleaning cups on the normal top shelf is beyond amazing and possibly the best feature I've ever seen in a dishwasher. Every little nook and cranny of a cup is cleared and the clips make sure they don't get blasted off the pins. The silverware specific jets have left our silverware so clean I didn't realize how scratched they had gotten. They are able to get all of the leftover debris off without issue. Peanut butter, jelly, mystery goo from something, all gone like it was nothing.Only complaint I have after a month of daily use is the front panel and handle notch. The section for the handle that you pull to open is flimsier than I would prefer. It has some play whenever you pull before the latch releases, but with all of the use it has not broken or appeared to begin breaking. Just something I was not expecting and would have though would be sturdier with the rest of the build quality on this.
